orchestrator_output.reformulated_query: Definition and explanation of uniform motion and non-uniform motion
orchestrator_output.text_narration:
• **Uniform Motion**: When an object moves along a straight path and covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, it is said to be in uniform motion.

• **Example of Uniform Motion**: A train traveling on a straight track at a constant speed that covers exactly 60 kilometers every single hour.

• **Non-Uniform Motion**: When an object covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time, it is said to be in non-uniform motion.

• **Example of Non-Uniform Motion**: A car moving through busy city traffic that stops at signal lights and changes speed, covering different distances every 10 minutes.

• **Main Difference**: In uniform motion, the speed of the object stays constant throughout the journey, whereas in non-uniform motion, the speed keeps changing.
